title: Midnight crumbs: latency spike triage and runbook TODOs
content:
Shift summary (11:45pm-07:45am)
- Pager at 00:18: high p50/p95 latency on hosted-api route /v1/generate for region us-west-2. Alerts: latency-frontend-high (p95 > 600ms), downstream error-rate bump.
- Initial blip lasted ~9 minutes, recurred at 00:39 and 01:05 with lower amplitude; stabilized after 01:20.

Immediate actions taken
- Acknowledged pager; pinged on-call infra (Liam) and alerts channel.
- Gathered quick context:
  * kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -> noticed 2 of 6 replicas with RESTARTS=1 and CPU at ~95% on node nvidia-gpu-05.
  * Prometheus graphing: host/vm_cpu_usage and container_cpu_user_seconds_total spike from 00:15-00:30.
  * Nginx logs: elevated upstream_connect_time and upstream_response_time; increased 502s intermittently.
  * Checked queue/backpressure: worker queue depth on generation queue spiked to 22k (normal ~600).
- Quick mitigation: scaled deployment hosted-api-gen to +3 replicas (kubectl scale --replicas=9 deployment/hosted-api-gen -n hosted-api). Backpressure drained in ~6 minutes, latency dropped to baseline.
- Evacuated pods on node nvidia-gpu-05: cordon+drain; node confirmed unhealthy for GPU driver (kernel OOM?). Opened node ticket to infra: INFRA-4521.

Hypothesis / probable root cause
- Node-level GPU driver/kernel instability led to several inference pods failing and CPU/queue pressure on remaining replicas. The autoscaler did not respond fast enough because horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) is based on CPU while the trigger was queue-depth/kind-of-inference-latency.
- Secondary contributor: a background batch job started at 00:10 that was not throttled properly and consumed shared GPU/CPU resources on the same node pool (job tag: batch-indexer-nightly).

Notes about runbooks and gaps found (quick list)
- Runbook "hosted-api-latency" has steps for pod restarts and scaling, but:
  * Missing quick checklist to check node GPU driver health and to cordon/evacuate nodes.
  * No play for queue-depth driven scaling. HPA docs mention CPU-based scaling only; need a sample KEDA/queue-backed autoscaler snippet.
  * Missing guidance for identifying and throttling background batch jobs that share GPU pool with serving.

Follow-ups / action items (owners + rough ETA)
- SRE: add queue-backed autoscaling example to runbook (owner: Nora) — ETA 2026-04-23. Ticket: SRE-PR-78.
- Infra: investigate node nvidia-gpu-05 crash (owner: Liam) — update in INFRA-4521, ETA 2026-04-21.
- Platform: add label enforcement so batch jobs do not schedule on serving GPU pool (owner: Priya) — create policy PR, ETA 2026-04-27.
- Product: review schedule of nightly batch-indexer; move heavy jobs to isolated pool or off-peak (owner: Aditya) — coordinate by 2026-04-30.
- Observability: add p95 latency alert that correlates with queue depth and a runbook link in the alert text (owner: Mei) — ETA 2026-04-22.

Commands used (copyable)
- kubectl -n hosted-api get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n hosted-api top pods --containers
- kubectl -n hosted-api scale deployment/hosted-api-gen --replicas=9
- kubectl cordon nvidia-gpu-05 && kubectl drain nvidia-gpu-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- curl -sS "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(container_cpu_user_seconds_total[5m])" | jq .

Runbook TODOs (quick prioritized list)
1) Add "check node GPU driver and cordon" section with exact commands, output examples, and decision tree. (priority: P0)
2) Add KEDA/queue-based HPA recipe and sample YAML (priority: P1)
3) Document how to mute background scheduled jobs or throttle for critical windows (priority: P1)
4) Put alerting links directly to runbook and to the ticket creation flow (priority: P2)
5) Add a small diagnostic script snippet to runbook to snapshot GPU processes and memory (nvidia-smi + docker ps) (priority: P2)

Open questions / unknowns to follow up on
- Why did autoscaler not trigger earlier? Check HPA config and CPU target; likely too conservative. Add historical HPA metrics to ticket.
- Confirm whether batch-indexer was co-located by label mistake or scheduler misconfiguration.
- Any kernel OOM logs for node? Ask infra to attach dmesg, kubelet logs.

Quick timeline (for postmortem draft)
- 00:12 background batch-indexer started
- 00:15 CPU/GPU driver errors begin on nvidia-gpu-05; some pods restart
- 00:18 alert fired (p95 > 600ms)
- 00:20 scaled hosted-api-gen +3 replicas (manual)
- 01:02 drained nvidia-gpu-05; queue drained by 01:10
- 01:20 latency baseline restored, monitoring watch until 02:30 then periodic checks until end of shift

Hand-off notes for next on-call
- INFRA-4521 is the main node ticket; expect updates from Liam.
- SRE-PR-78 (runbook + autoscaler) is in my queue — please pick up if you have bandwidth.
- If latency recurs, check queue depth before scalings and consider immediate manual scale if queue > 5k.

Misc quick scribbles
- Consider adding a "serving-only" node taint for GPU pool so batch jobs need explicit toleration.
- Think about short-term: increase HPA cooldown to react faster? or lower CPU threshold? Risk: thrash. Better: queue-driven autoscaler.

End of notes.
summary: Night shift triage for hosted-api latency spike caused by GPU node instability + noisy batch job. Manual scale and node drain mitigated. Runbook gaps identified (node GPU checks, queue-based autoscaling). Follow-ups assigned to SRE/Infra/Platform/Observability.
